title: Derived Hom from a bounded-above projective complex
statement: Let R be a ring and regard it as the structure ring of the one-point ringed site, with derived category D(R) defined by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let P^\bullet be a bounded-above cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] of projective R-modules [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective], and let L^\bullet be a bounded-below cochain complex of R-modules. Then the ordinary Hom complex Hom_R^\bullet(P^\bullet,L^\bullet), whose degree-n term is \prod_p Hom_R(P^p,L^{p+n}), represents the derived Hom R Hom_R(P^\bullet,L^\bullet) obtained by specializing [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] to this one-point ringed site. In particular its cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees.

source.place: Tag 0GM8, lemma-stalk-internal-hom, case (2), together with the K-projective construction of derived Hom

proof.text: On the one-point bottom-topology site, evaluation is faithful and exact. The slice over the point is again a singleton. Identify sections of internal Hom with module maps on this slice. Kernels are preserved by Hom. Extend a point map to a sheaf morphism and lift it through the given epimorphism using categorical projectivity of P.X p. Restrict this lift back to the point. Thus internal Hom from each term of P preserves short exact sequences, without any finite-generation assumption. This is proved directly by private helpers in the item module.

For a quasi-isomorphism between bounded-below targets M,N and a fixed homology degree n, cut P below k=min(aM,aN)-n-1. Below k the target factors of the Hom product vanish in degrees n-1,n,n+1; above k the truncation inclusion is an isomorphism. The product-limit projections therefore show that cutting P preserves Hom homology in degree n. The cut source is bounded and has exact internal Hom in every term, so apply quasiIso_homComplex_map_of_bounded_exact_terms. Naturality and two-out-of-three give the desired quasi-isomorphism in degree n for P.

Choose a bounded-below K-injective resolution beta:M→T by exists_boundedBelow_injective_resolution. The preceding step applies to beta. Compare with the canonical functorial replacement eta:M→F(M) through the naturality square for beta. F(beta) and eta at T are quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives, and Hom(P,-) preserves these by quasiIso_homComplex_map. Two-out-of-three proves the Hom comparison for eta at M. Apply the naturality square again to an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism M→I with I K-injective to obtain its Hom comparison, even if I is not bounded below.

The derived localization Q inverts the Hom comparison for any functorial replacement, proving the universal comparison clause. Compose its canonical instance with the inverse component of derivedInternalHom_comparison to represent derived Hom by Q Hom(P,L). Finally take a=e-d. If n<a, each product factor Hom(P^p,L^q), with p+n=q, is zero: either p>d or q<e. Product-limit extensionality makes the degree-n term zero, hence its homology zero.

lean.statement: theorem affineProjectiveComplexDerivedHom {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose ⊥ (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf R)))] (P L : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose ⊥ (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf R))) ℤ) (d e : ℤ) [P.IsStrictlyLE d] [L.IsStrictlyGE e] [∀ n : ℤ, Projective (P.X n)] : Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (homComplex (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf R) P L) ≅ (derivedInternalHom ⊥ (CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf R)).obj (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P), DerivedCategory.Q.obj L)) ∧ (∀ (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose ⊥ (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf R))) ℤ ⥤ CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose ⊥ (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf R))) ℤ) (η : 𝟭 (CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose ⊥ (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf R))) ℤ) ⟶ I), (∀ N : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose ⊥ (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf R))) ℤ, QuasiIso (η.app N) ∧ (I.obj N).IsKInjective) → IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map (((homComplexFunctor (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf R)).obj (op P)).map (η.app L)))) ∧ ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a → IsZero ((homComplex (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf R) P L).homology n)
